title: No punishment without a law
summary: You can only be punished for something that was already a defined offence, with a set penalty, at the time you did it.
body_plain: The Constitution says no one can be convicted of a criminal offence unless that offence is defined, and the penalty prescribed, in a written law. You also cannot be punished more heavily than the penalty that was in force when the offence was committed. This means the authorities cannot invent an offence after the fact or increase your punishment retroactively.
rights: You can only be convicted of an offence defined in a written law (s.36(12)).
You cannot be given a heavier penalty than the one in force when you acted (s.36(8)).
Offences and penalties cannot be applied retroactively against you.
do_list: Ask which specific written law you are accused of breaking.
Tell your lawyer if the 'offence' is not clearly written in law.
Keep note of the exact charge.
dont_list: Do not accept a charge that is not based on a clear written law.
Do not accept a penalty heavier than the law allowed at the time.
common_situations: You are threatened with punishment for conduct that was not an offence when it occurred.
A charge does not identify a written law or clearly defined offence.
A later, harsher penalty is being applied to earlier conduct.
words_to_use: What written law created this offence at the time of the alleged conduct?
Please identify the exact charge and penalty in writing.
I need legal advice before responding to an allegation that is not clearly defined.
if_violated: Keep the charge, alleged date, cited law, penalty notice, and every version of the relevant rule.
Do not rely only on verbal descriptions; ask your lawyer to compare the conduct date with the law then in force.
Raise the issue through the proper court process rather than ignoring a summons or charge.

citations.source_name: 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
